title: OpenAI announced a model it would not release.
description:
OpenAI announced a model it would not release. 'Due to our concerns about malicious applications of the technology, we are not releasing the trained model.'

It had 1.5 billion parameters. It was trained on 8 million web pages with one job: predict the next word.

It never was. A much smaller model and a technical paper went out the same day. A 345 million parameter version followed in May 2019.

The full model was released anyway. OpenAI said: 'We've seen no strong evidence of misuse so far.'

Called the release 'a test case of a full staged release process'.

The model too dangerous to release was public within the year.

Sources:
- https://openai.com/index/better-language-models/ - OpenAI's February 2019 announcement; established 1.5 billion parameters, 8 million web pages of training data, the next-word objective, the quote 'we are not releasing the trained model', and that a much smaller model and a paper were released instead.
- https://openai.com/index/gpt-2-1-5b-release/ - OpenAI's 5 November 2019 post; established the full 1.5B release as the final stage, the phrase 'a test case of a full staged release process', and 'We've seen no strong evidence of misuse so far.'
